detail.abstract: This technical white paper introduces the Global Corporate Threat Intelligence (GCTI™) framework, a proprietary applied intelligence methodology developed by Jose Parejo & Associates (JPA). The framework addresses a persistent structural gap in corporate risk advisory: the disconnect between macro-level geopolitical forecasting and the operationally precise intelligence required for boardroom decision-making. Drawing on field experience across more than 100 countries and five continents, the paper argues that the primary failure mode in corporate geopolitical risk is not analytical depth, but the absence of structured methods for translating intelligence into actionable governance outputs. The GCTI™ framework resolves this through the systematic deployment of Structured Analytic Techniques (SATs) — including Analysis of Competing Hypotheses (ACH), Premortem Disruption Modeling, and High-Impact/Low-Probability Threat Assessments — originally developed within Western sovereign intelligence communities and codified in CIA and ODNI analytical standards. The paper situates the GCTI™ framework within the broader transatlantic risk advisory landscape alongside institutional counterparts including Eurasia Group, McLarty Associates, and the US Army War College Strategic Studies Institute, establishing a clear methodological position for boutique applied intelligence as a complementary and distinct capability. Outputs of the framework are designed to be legally defensible, auditable, and directly usable in international dispute resolution, asset protection, and multi-jurisdictional compliance. This document is registered for open-access indexing via SSRN and Zenodo and forms part of the permanent methodological corpus of Jose Parejo & Associates.

title: From Traits to Troubles: Exploring CEO Personality and Adverse Financial Restatements
affiliations: , ,  and University of Georgia - Terry College of Business

detail.title: From Traits to Troubles: Exploring CEO Personality and Adverse Financial Restatements
detail.abstract: The personality of CEOs is increasingly garnering attention as it relates to the accounting discipline due to the documented impact on important firm level outcomes. In this work, we examine the role of CEOs Big Five Personality traits on the occurrence and severity of adverse financial restatements. Leveraging machine and deep learning techniques, we first extract CEO personality scores from the audio, visual, and text features of videos. These scores are then used to advance understanding surrounding the relationship between CEO personality and adverse financial restatements of firms, controlling for firm and CEO characteristics. Results reveal that CEO extraversion is the most robust indicator of adverse financial restatements, increasing the likelihood of their occurrence. When adverse financial restatements occur, CEO neuroticism and conscientiousness reduce their severity as proxied by negative market reactions. These results underscore how CEO personality may shape the financial reporting of firms.

title: A Convex Reformulation of the Deribit Portfolio Margin Model: A Note

detail.title: A Convex Reformulation of the Deribit Portfolio Margin Model: A Note

declarations.funderStatement: No funding.

detail.abstract: We present a convex portfolio margin model for derivatives exchanges and show that convexity enables a unified treatment of three core risk problems: margin computation, liquidation, and auto-deleveraging (ADL). The margin requirement is a single convex function of portfolio positions: the worst-case loss ρ max over a grid of spot and implied-volatility scenarios, augmented by a roll-risk adjustment via full repricing and a linear surcharge for concentrated positions. Convexity reduces minimum-cost liquidation and fair ADL to tractable convex programmes with global-optimality guarantees. We contrast this with the portfolio margin model of Deribit, the leading crypto options exchange, and identify two structural issues: additive delta-and roll-risk overlays driven by a signmasked offset that is non-convex in positions, and a roll-risk approximation that is first-order in delta and misses gamma-driven exposure near expiry. The convex framework eliminates both while remaining simple to implement and audit.

detail.abstract: The Trump Administration’s tariff strategy has entered a time-sensitive phase. After the Supreme Court ruling limited the use of emergency economic powers as a basis for broad tariff measures, the Administration turned to other statutory authorities to preserve tariff leverage. The most immediate instrument was a temporary global surcharge under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974. Section 122, however, permits an import surcharge of up to 15 percent for a period not exceeding 150 days unless extended by Congress. July 24, 2026, thus serves as an important statutory reference point for assessing how the Administration may seek to maintain tariff leverage after the temporary surcharge expires.

title: Comparative Analysis of Initial and Long-term Financial Commitments of Cloud-based and Onpremises Infrastructure Solutions for Large Language Models

detail.title: Comparative Analysis of Initial and Long-term Financial Commitments of Cloud-based and Onpremises Infrastructure Solutions for Large Language Models
detail.abstract: The rapid advancements in artificial intelligence and deep learning, particularly in Large Language Models (LLMs), have significantly increased computational demands for organizations. This paper provides a comparative analysis of the initial and long-term financial commitments associated with cloud-based and on-premises infrastructure solutions for deploying LLMs across organizations of varying sizes. It examines the costefficiency, environmental impact, and required skill sets for managing these infrastructures. The study employs a mixed-methods approach, including a comprehensive literature review and a workshop involving students from a master's program in Business Information Systems. Key findings indicate that cloud-based solutions offer lower upfront costs and scalability, making them suitable for startups and small to medium-sized enterprises, while on-premises solutions provide greater control and potentially lower long-term costs, beneficial for larger organizations with specific compliance and data security needs. Additionally, the study highlights cost-reduction strategies such as transfer learning, sparse training, and optimal hyperparameter tuning. The results aim to guide organizations in aligning their infrastructure strategies with technical needs, financial constraints, and environmental responsibilities, thereby future proofing their investments in LLM deployment.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a dynamic equilibrium model of U.S. Treasury clearing that endogenizes explicit, VaR-based initial margins, EWMA volatility updates, variation-margin feedback, cross-margining, and crowding effects within CCP competition. We cast clearing as a threestage stochastic game: CCPs commit to fees, margin multipliers, cross-margin discounts, and volatility-decay parameters; members allocate DV01 exposures in each period subject to funding-cost feedback from margin calls; and CCPs incur tail-risk, covariance, concentration, and infrastructure penalties over time. In the symmetric competitive equilibrium, stronger cross-margining discounts, dynamically calibrated skin-in-the-game buffers, concentration surcharges, and conservative margin-and-volatility regimes all reduce the joint default probability. We benchmark against a single-CCP monopoly and demonstrate that only under extreme crowding does a well-capitalized monopoly dominate. Our comparativestatics yield a comprehensive policy toolkit-transparent margin formulas, volatility-decay standards, feedback-cap mechanisms, cross-margin interoperability, and real-time crowding metrics-to guide resilient Treasury clearing.

title: Inside Information in Protracted Processes after the Listing Act: End of the Story?
affiliations: University of Genoa - Law Department and Centre for Law and Finance and

detail.title: Inside Information in Protracted Processes after the Listing Act: End of the Story?

publicationDetails.detailsText: European Corporate Governance Institute - Law Working Paper No. 944/2026
publicationDetails.journalName: European Corporate Governance Institute (ECGI) - Law Working Paper Series

detail.abstract:
The Listing Act marks a significant turning point in the European regulation of inside information by reshaping the treatment of protracted processes under MAR. Moving away from the original framework developed in Geltl v. Daimler, the new regime adopts a clearer two-step model that separates the prohibition of insider dealing from the issuer’s duty of disclosure. While leaving the insider trading ban untouched, for protracted processes the new regime postpones disclosure until the occurrence of the final event. This reform aims to reduce the regulatory burden for listed companies and to reduce disclosure of preliminary information.

Our paper shows, however, that the Listing Act does not fully eliminate legal uncertainty. Although the Commission Delegated Regulation provides a more detailed taxonomy of protracted processes and identifies numerous examples of “final events,” the dividing line separating protracted processes and one-off events is a matter of interpretation and can occasionally raise doubts on its consequences. Following ESMA’s technical advice, the Commission Delegated Regulation confines the concept of protracted processes to developments that depend, at least in part, on the issuer’s own actions or decisions. This criterion leaves some questions concerning the boundaries of the new rules unresolved. One first question relates to the rationale for subjecting disclosure of external developments that evolve progressively over time to the old regime. A second question revolves around the treatment of inside information within corporate groups, including whether events occurring in controlled entities shall be treated as protracted processes or one-off events from the perspective of listed companies. A third question concerns disclosure relating to accounting data revealing profit warnings and earnings surprises.

Overall, the new regime will likely have a positive impact in that it increases certainty concerning the timing of disclosure for protracted processes, including periodic financial reports. However, substantial interpretive discretion remains regarding the treatment of external events, the organisation of internal information systems, and the identification of the corporate actors whose knowledge is attributable to the issuer. The actual impact of the new rules on these matters will, therefore, crucially depend on the interpretation by issuers, supervisors, and ultimately courts.

title: Commercial Short Video Adoption: Examining interrelationship between Antecedents, Mediators and Consequences

detail.title: Commercial Short Video Adoption: Examining interrelationship between Antecedents, Mediators and Consequences
detail.abstract:
Short videos have become really popular in past few years and have emerged as a revolutionary tool in digital marketing, influencer marketing, brand awareness and purchase decisions. This study investigates the key factors driving Commercial Short Video Adoption (CSVA) and focuses on the impact of Entertainment Value (EV), Information Seeking (IS), Ease of Access (EA) and Social Interaction (SI) with User Engagement (UE) as a mediating factor. Also, Age and Gender were examined as moderating variables to assess the effect of demographics in short video consumption.
In this study, a quantitative approach was used where an online survey was exercised to collect responses from 212 participants. The data was analysed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) in SmartPLS, reliability testing, normality testing, correlation analysis and multiple regression models in SPSS. The results revealed that IS, EA and SI have positive impact on UE which also have a strong relation with CSVA. However, EV does not have a significant effect on UE therefore it alone cannot be suggested as the primary motivator for consumption of commercial short videos.
Furthermore, the study confirms that CSVA has positive influence on both Purchase Intention (PI) and Brand Awareness (BA) which gives a favourable view of the effectiveness of short video marketing. Also, Gender influences the effect of EA on CSVA with women being more affected, while Age moderates the effect of SI on CSVA with older users engaging more through social interaction.
These findings provide valuable insights which can be used by marketers, businesses and brands looking to use short videos as a part of their marketing strategies. It also implies that businesses should prioritize informative and interactive content, ensure ease of access and leverage social engagement tools to maximize consumer adoption and conversion of potential customers. The study also contributes to marketing literature and Uses and Gratifications Theory (UGT) in the context of commercial short video adoption.
Despite its contributions, the study also has certain limitations. Future research should explore longitudinal studies for extended periods, cross platform comparisons and AI-driven personalization in short video engagement.

title: Analyst Forecast Biases and the Cost of Wishful Thinking
affiliations: University of Michigan at Ann Arbor - Finance, INSEAD and INSEAD

detail.title: Analyst Forecast Biases and the Cost of Wishful Thinking
detail.abstract: We show that EPS forecasts exhibit underreaction and CAPEX forecasts exhibit overreaction, both at the individual and consensus levels, for the same analysts and firms. Standard models cannot reconcile this. We propose a wishful thinking model of forecasts in which analysts optimally distort beliefs about signal precision to gain anticipatory utility. A single parameter, the cost of belief distortion, generates both biases: high costs produce underreaction, low costs produce overreaction, and intermediate costs yield individual overreaction but consensus underreaction. The model further predicts that overreaction is stronger at longer horizons and among more experienced analysts, and that low-cost environments feature greater forecast dispersion and consensus volatility. We confirm these predictions in the data.

title: Epistemic Climate in Corporate Governance: A Two-Axis Diagnostic Framework for Board Decision Quality
affiliations: Straticom Technologies Sàrl

detail.title: Epistemic Climate in Corporate Governance: A Two-Axis Diagnostic Framework for Board Decision Quality

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder of Straticom Technologies Sàrl and the developer of the instruments described in this paper. No external funding was received.

detail.abstract: The governance diagnostic literature has developed substantially over three decades in its capacity to describe board dysfunction — the patterns of communication, composition, and process failure that characterise boards in difficulty. It has developed considerably less in its capacity to explain that dysfunction: to identify the causal conditions that produce governance failure before it becomes visible in outcomes. This paper introduces the Board Decision Climate Profile™ (BDC Profile™) and the Chair Epistemic Behaviour Instrument™ (CEBI™), two diagnostic instruments designed to measure the epistemic conditions under which boards make decisions. Drawing on peer-reviewed research in psychological safety (Edmondson, 1999, 2018), group cognition and hidden information (Forbes & Milliken, 1999; Stasser & Titus, 1985), cognitive diversity activation (Page, 2007; Reynolds & Lewis, 2017), and structured dissent (Janis, 1972; Sunstein & Hastie, 2015), we propose a two-axis governance climate model — Epistemic Safety and Cognitive Activation — whose intersection produces four Board Decision Climate States. The CEBI extends the framework by attributing climate state variation to the chair's specific epistemic behaviours across three dimensions: Invitation Behaviour, Safety Modelling, and Activation Practice. Together, the BDC Profile and CEBI constitute the second and third stages of the Complete Governance Climate Diagnostic™, a three-instrument sequence designed to move board assessment from pattern description to causal diagnosis. We document the theoretical foundations, construct architecture, instrument design, scoring logic, and a formal validation programme. Research limitations and future directions are identified.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a longitudinal practitioner case study of digital transformation executed across two regulated, high-volume sectors in Saudi Arabia: telecommunications (2012 to 2023) and consumer finance (2023 to present). Drawing on eleven years of direct operational and architectural leadership, the study examines how structural redesign, early eligibility gating, unified channel logic, and lifecycle governance converge to produce sustainable digital throughput in compliance-constrained environments. The central contribution is the Structured Velocity Operating Framework, a five-pillar conceptual model encompassing architectural decoupling, early eligibility gating, unified channel logic, operational intelligence, and lifecycle governance. Empirical evidence drawn from production deployments demonstrates measurable improvements across key performance dimensions: personal finance turnaround time reduced from approximately six to approximately two calendar days; application submission conversion increased from 71% to 95%; digital origination share reached approximately 95% of all business transactions; and post-redesign registrations grew approximately 3.8 times within a seven-month window. The paper argues that sustainable digital advantage in regulated financial institutions derives not from speed alone but from the institutional capacity to govern velocity across the full customer lifecycle. The findings are contextualized within Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 financial sector transformation agenda and the rapid expansion of the Kingdom's fintech ecosystem from 82 licensed entities in 2021 to over 280 by 2025. The Structured Velocity Framework is presented as a transferable operating model for regulated institutions seeking to reconcile transformation urgency with governance discipline.

detail.abstract: In this study, we use the 2005-2019 TurkStat Household Labor Force Surveys to examine the changes in worker flows in Turkey and how different demographic groups are affected by these changes. We then estimate wage differentials between workers who started their current job within the last 12 months and those who have been employed in the same job for more than a year, taking tenure into account. Our descriptive analyses indicate that, due to the increase in worker turnover, labor market stratification has deepened, and a group of workers appears to be trapped in a cycle of temporary/low-quality jobs and unemployment. Regarding the impact of changes in worker flows on wages, our findings show that workers who changed jobs within the last 12 months earn lower wages compared to those who remained in their ongoing jobs. Moreover, our results suggest that when the returns to experience are high, job switching may become more costly.

title: Spatial Competition and Temporal Price Discrimination in Brazilian Street Markets
affiliations: Delta Economics & Finance

detail.title: Spatial Competition and Temporal Price Discrimination in Brazilian Street Markets
detail.abstract: I develop a unified equilibrium framework to explain the systematic pricing patterns observed in Brazilian street markets (feiras livres). Two contrasting market structures coexist within the same physical space: a perishable produce market, in which prices decline from dawn to noon and quality is positively associated with neighborhood income, and a market for the complementary treats pastel and caldo de cana, characterized by intraday price rigidity, spatial price dispersion, and lower prices on weekdays. For produce I construct a two-period adverse-selection model where sellers possess private quality information and face heterogeneous early-selling costs; rational-expectations equilibrium yields a declining price path and income-based quality sorting. For treats I first examine a Hotelling duopoly with an outside option, which explains income-sensitive price levels and the weekday-weekend differential but fails to deliver intra-market price dispersion. I then develop a Varian-type model with a nested loyalty structure of informed shoppers and uninformed locals, treating the two goods as perfect complements. This second treats model endogenously generates price dispersion across the poles of a market, sharpens the weekday-discount mechanism, and incorporates cross-market competitive pressure from cosmopolitan consumers. The two core models-adverse selection for produce and mixed-strategy spatial competition for treats-are complementary and jointly rationalize the full set of stylized facts.

title: Pre-Construction Governance Failures in Municipal Infrastructure: A Practitioner Case Study from Tarash Municipality, Bangladesh

detail.title: Pre-Construction Governance Failures in Municipal Infrastructure: A Practitioner Case Study from Tarash Municipality, Bangladesh
detail.abstract: This paper examines two municipal road construction projects in Tarash Municipality, Sirajganj district, Bangladesh that experienced avoidable implementation delays during the 2023-2024 Annual Development Programme cycle. Drawing on municipal project files, contractor correspondence, engineering documentation, land records, and the author's direct experience as Administrator of the municipality, the study asks why projects that followed standard procurement procedures still encountered significant delays. The answer in both cases was the same: problems that were administratively knowable before tendering, roadside encroachment in one project, a government pond lease and boundary dispute in another, were not identified until after the contractor had mobilised. This produced delays of four and three months respectively, not because the problems were complex but because their late discovery forced design revisions, inter-agency coordination, and re-approval processes that could have been completed at the preparation stage at far lower cost. The paper argues that for smaller Bangladeshi municipalities, the weakest link in infrastructure delivery is pre-construction governance, the institutional tasks of mapping land use, engaging affected stakeholders, and coordinating with other agencies before a tender is issued. These tasks are not always systematically incorporated into local project preparation practices and may depend significantly on administrative discretion. Making them a formal, documented step in the ADP project cycle would reduce avoidable delays without requiring new institutions or significant additional resources.

detail.abstract: Battery energy storage (BESS) is widely considered essential for decarbonising power systems. In this research, we test whether short-term electricity price arbitrage generates sufficient returns to justify investment and BESS economic viability across four interconnected Central and Eastern European day-ahead markets-Romania, Bulgaria, Hungary, and the Czech Republic-from 2018 to 2024, accounting for realistic forecasting uncertainty. All four markets exhibit volatile, heavy-tailed prices and a pronounced daily price seasonality, creating opportunities for arbitrage. We generate joint probabilistic price forecasts using DRF (distributional random forests) and translate these into dayahead battery bidding decisions under real operating constraints. We compare performance with naïve and perfect-foresight benchmarks using standard investment metrics. Empirical findings confirm that probabilistic forecasting adds clear operational value, outperforming a fixed-schedule strategy in every market. The largest gains are seen in the Czech Republic and Bulgaria. Operating a battery in a cross-border setup generates additional profit, driven by persistent regional price differences rather than broad diversification. However, neither forecasting skill nor cross-market flexibility alone is sufficient to make the investment profitable. Therefore, current Li-ion BESS costs make realistic capital recovery unlikely, indicating that deeper market integration, cost reduction and additional revenue streams are necessary for viability.

We present a comparison of data with other economies, as China, Japan and some European countries, regarding some indicators of development and welfate. We include references to some interesting econometric models of Employment by sector in India and in other countries and we focus on the trends to diminution of Farm Employment and increase in Non Farm Employment. detail.abstract: This paper argues that Japan's contemporary transformation is best understood not as a voluntary return to militarism or a simple continuation of postwar passivity, but as a forced adaptation to the externalization of its own economic system. Postwar Japan functioned as a security-outsourced economic state: the United States supplied the hard infrastructure of regional security while Japan specialized in manufacturing, technology, finance, export competitiveness, and domestic social organization. That settlement is now under pressure because Japan's economic reproduction increasingly depends on external energy routes, production networks, critical minerals, semiconductor chains, maritime corridors, labor channels, and overseas assets. The paper develops a conditional mechanism: externalized economy produces pressure for externalized security when external inputs become costly to substitute, domestic reproductive capacity weakens, and the state possesses sufficient institutional capacity to act outward. The Japanese case is therefore not only a story of threat response. It is a case of economic externalization becoming a security problem. Historical comparison clarifies the mechanism. Similar Japan-Asia-Pacific complementarities were channeled in the 1930s through depression, protectionism, military autonomy, and revisionist order-building into coercive empire. Contemporary Japan faces different channeling conditions: higher legitimacy constraints, alliance embedding, partner agency, supply-chain security, and the high cost of war. The result is not territorial command, but movement toward a security-industrial state, a networked stabilizer, and a new layer of financial recognition.

detail.abstract: We develop DoEx, a firm-quarter measure of currency exposure, built from how intensively managers and analysts discuss the currency environment—exchange-rate levels, volatility, and the dollar’s direction—on quarterly earnings conference calls for 8,294 U.S.-listed firms over 2007–2024. DoEx tracks every major dollar episode of the period and rises with firms’ real international footprints, and carries information well beyond alternative currency-exposure proxies, including foreign-sales ratios and return-based FX betas. Firms with higher exposure experience equity-price declines when the dollar appreciates, and they act on this exposure by using more FX derivatives and tilting their borrowing toward non-USD-denominated debt.

detail.abstract: Autonomous agent ecosystems operating at civilizational scale require a trust layer that does not exist in contemporary agentic stacks. Identity protocols establish who an agent is. Permission systems gate what an agent may execute. Neither addresses how trust propagates between agents across a decentralized mesh without a central authority. This paper introduces DTPP-Ω (Decentralized Trust Propagation Protocol, Omega Architecture), a protocol designed to operate across the period 2026-2100. DTPP-Ω is built on eleven constitutional invariants, nine architectural components, a two-phase authorization engine, a bounded trust budget system, an influence graph layer, and a fully specified sentinel governance mechanism. The protocol's core design objective is trustworthy operation under uncertainty-not maximum trust, but bounded, explainable, auditable, locally computed, influence-aware trust that degrades gracefully under adversarial conditions. The architecture is motivated by back casting analysis identifying the absence of an inter-agent trust propagation layer as a probable cause of hypothesized civilizational-scale alignment failures between 2039 and 2042.

detail.abstract: In this paper, we study the emergence and elimination of arbitrage opportunities in computerized limit order markets. We measure price changes, buy/sell market/limit order submissions/cancellations at message frequency during arbitrage opportunities in NYMEX WTI futures and options using their model-free no-arbitrage relation. We find that executed arbitrage trades in all three markets during the life of an arbitrage opportunity are virtually nonexistent. In the more liquid futures market, executed trades eliminate arbitrage, whereas in the options markets, liquidity providers are the ones who correct arbitrage opportunities. These results highlight the critical role of liquidity providers in maintaining price efficiency.

detail.title: The Beautiful Game And The Inattentive Market: Global Culture, the FIFA World Cup, and Investor Attention in the U.S. Stock Market
detail.abstract: The FIFA World Cup is the most watched sporting event in human history, drawing over five billion viewers globally across its tournament weeks. Its economic footprint is staggering: the 2026 edition, hosted across the United States, Canada, and Mexico, is projected to generate up to $80 billion in global gross output and $40.9 billion in global GDP impact. Yet alongside this extraordinary commercial vitality lies a paradox of profound importance for financial economists: the same cultural phenomenon that generates billions in revenue appears to simultaneously withdraw investor attention from financial markets, compressing trading volume, depressing market sentiment, and producing measurable negative abnormal returns in the U.S. stock market during the tournament months of June and July. This paper examines the dual economic identity of the FIFA World Cup, as a generator of global commercial activity and as a systematic disruptor of investor attention. We review the theoretical foundations of limited attention in financial markets, survey the empirical literature on the World Cup effect across national equity markets, analyze the specific dynamics of U.S. market behavior during World Cup months compared to equivalent non-World Cup periods, and document the channels through which the tournament transmits its effects: sentiment, distraction, and gambling spillover. Our findings contribute to behavioral finance by framing the World Cup as a natural experiment in mass cognitive reallocation with predictable, measurable, and exploitable financial consequences.

title: SOVEREIGN Counsel: Attributable Judgment, Fractional Models, and NULL Drift in Legal Services

detail.title: SOVEREIGN Counsel: Attributable Judgment, Fractional Models, and NULL Drift in Legal Services
detail.abstract:
This paper applies the Burgess Principle's binary test — SOVEREIGN, where a named human mind demonstrably applied judgment to the specific facts of a matter before an output issued; NULL, where no such application can be evidenced — to legal services. Legal representation occupies a distinctive position in the framework: it is the professional layer most often asked to convert institutional NULL gaps into owned decisions, and is therefore the layer whose own attributability matters most.

The paper operationalizes the test for solicitor work, specifying four evidentiary markers that constitute demonstrated application of judgment and establishing who is positioned to score them. It then identifies the structural drivers of NULL drift in traditional engagements — volume incentives, template correspondence, delegation without recorded review, and failure to engage client-specific constraints, including Equality Act 2010 reasonable adjustments. These dynamics are illustrated through an abstracted composite engagement drawn from a documented instructed relationship.

The fractional or project-scoped solicitor model is examined as a structurally higher-SOVEREIGN-density alternative, with the evidentiary basis and rival explanations stated explicitly. A five-element remediation protocol, adapted from the framework's prior application to institutional failure, allows any client to score an engagement for SOVEREIGN compliance. A concluding analysis extends the test to machine-assisted self-representation, arguing that the self-represented litigant operating a record-complete, constraint-embodying workflow satisfies the test's authorship requirement in its purest available form. The paper concludes that legal services must themselves be capable of passing the test they are routinely asked to enforce on others.

title: Differential Ire: Why Attributable Governance Harms Sustain Public Accountability Pressure That Diffuse Scandals Do Not: An Application of the Burgess Principle

detail.title: Differential Ire: Why Attributable Governance Harms Sustain Public Accountability Pressure That Diffuse Scandals Do Not: An Application of the Burgess Principle
detail.abstract: This paper examines an observable asymmetry in public response to institutional harm. Harms that the public can trace to identifiable human decisions-a sign-off, a refusal, an operational choice made at a discrete moment-generate accountability pressure that is more intense, more durable, and more institutionally consequential than harms of equal or greater aggregate magnitude that remain diffuse. The paper applies the Burgess Principle's binary test (SOVEREIGN: a named human mind demonstrably applied to the specific facts; NULL: no such application can be evidenced) as a descriptive instrument for predicting which harms enter the first category. Two historical clusters (Grenfell Tower, Hillsborough, the infected blood scandal, and the Post Office Horizon scandal, contrasted with the Madoff fraud and the opioid epidemic) and one contemporary case-the murder of Henry Nowak in Southampton in December 2025 and the subsequent scrutiny of the police response-are reviewed strictly on the established public record. The Horizon scandal is treated as a boundary case that refines the thesis: durability of public ire tracks the combination of attributability and irrecoverability of harm, with death the limiting instance of irrecoverability rather than a separate variable. The paper argues throughout that NULL is a measurement, not an accusation: it identifies where no named judgment can be evidenced, and predicts that such gaps, once attached to irrecoverable harm, become focal points of sustained public ire. The paper closes with a five-element remediation protocol-stated generally, so that any institution's post-failure response can itself be scored SOVEREIGN or NULL-before addressing limitations, alternative explanations, and the risk of political co-option of attributable cases.

detail.title: Investment Decisions, Voluntary Disclosure, Myopia, and Bounded Inefficiency
detail.abstract: We study a voluntary disclosure setting in which a manager privately observes the values of two mutually exclusive projects, only one of which generates verifiable and disclosable short-term information. The disclosable project offers an option value that the non-disclosable project does not, so myopic incentives tilt project choice toward the disclosable project. We show that even when the manager cares almost exclusively about the short-term price, the efficiency loss is small relative to the first-best outcome. By identifying conditions under which short-term pricing pressure has limited real consequences, the model may explain why empirical estimates of myopia-induced investment distortions are often small.

detail.abstract:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming healthcare. While the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the marketing of more than 1,400 AI-based products classified as devices under Section 201(h)(1) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, many other AI-based products, including certain clinical decision support (CDS) software tools that provide recommendations to health care professionals about diagnosis, treatment, or prevention of a disease or condition, have been placed on the U.S. market without FDA premarket review. On January 6, 2026, the FDA issued a revised CDS Guidance, which superseded the September 28, 2022 CDS Guidance. Shortly after, the agency issued the January 29, 2026 CDS Guidance, which superseded the January 6, 2026 CDS Guidance.

This Article systematically examines and compares three versions of the CDS Guidance: (1) the 2022 CDS Guidance, (2) the January 6, 2026 CDS Guidance, and (3) the January 29, 2026 CDS Guidance. It identifies key changes between the three versions and analyzes their implications for CDS using AI (AI-based CDS). In particular, this Article argues that since the 2022 CDS Guidance, the FDA’s overall trend has been to expand the scope of AI-based CDS that do not meet the device definition and of those that are devices but for which the agency intends to exercise enforcement discretion. As a result, an increasing number of AI-based CDS, including Generative AI-based CDS, can enter the U.S. market without FDA premarket review, leading to a lack of transparency as well as safety and effectiveness concerns.

title: The Fragility of Semi-Liquid Private Credit Funds

detail.title: The Fragility of Semi-Liquid Private Credit Funds
detail.abstract: We study fragility in semi-liquid private credit funds, which have expanded rapidly and now manage over $300 billion in assets. These funds perform liquidity transformation by holding far more illiquid loans than traditional loan mutual funds while allowing investors to redeem at NAV through quarterly repurchase offers, typically capped at 5% of shares outstanding. We show that cash buffers and contractual loan repayments are insufficient to fund repeated 5% quarterly redemptions; inflows decline precisely when outflows rise; and net outflows are met with sales of illiquid loans, external borrowing, and delayed payments through repurchases payable. As a result, strategic complementarity arises, because redemptions impose liquidation and leverage costs on the remaining investors. We show that loan liquidation, leverage increase, and NAV inflation play an important role in amplifying the current episodes of run-like redemptions. Overall, our evidence suggests that quarterly gates and redemption caps do not eliminate run-like fragility in semi-liquid private credit funds, raising cautions about expanding retail access to private credit markets.

detail.abstract: The research question aims to present the current state of the CE in NUTS 2 regions within France and Italy, top circularity performers in the EU, aiming to highlight the relationships and patterns among the reduce, reuse, recycle and socioeconomic indicators used to describe the circular economy, and to identify opportune instruments/policies to keep materials and products in circulation for as long as possible and to ensure sustainable development. This necessitates the definition of new development models and leads to decision problems in the public sector. To achieve this, understanding the socioeconomic and environmental situation of a territorial area is vital. Using Eurostat indicators and considering disposal and recovery facilities' numbers, a composite index (Waste Index) is identified and used as a decision attribute, alongside sustainability indicators as conditional attributes within the Multi-Attribute Analysis framework. This way, relationships and patterns are expressed as decision rules. Specific indicators in the decision rules, especially in the "reduce" analysis, like fertilizers and water-induced soil erosion, are crucial. Surprisingly, in the "reuse" analysis, the number of businesses for repairing computers and vehicles appears infrequently. When considering economic and social aspect, attributes like broadband access and tertiary education play significant roles in decision rules, while the employment rate never appears.

detail.title: The Price of Carry: Funding Frictions, Parity Failures, and Crash Risk
detail.abstract: Building on Brunnermeier et al. (2009), we show that FX carry remains profitable in a broad USD-funded universe, but post-2006 performance is weaker and strongly left-tailed. UIP failures explain the average premium: high-yield currencies do not depreciate enough to offset interest-rate differentials. CIP deviations reveal when those returns become fragile: after Lehman's collapse, the cross-currency basis turns structurally negative, and larger dislocations predict future downside asymmetry. Option-implied moments add ex ante evidence that funding stress and crash risk are priced before they materialize. Sovereign bond carry does not improve the trade-off, as duration and yield-curve risks are poorly compensated.

detail.abstract: This paper provides a preliminary analysis of the ILO Decent Work in the Platform Economy Convention, 2026 (No. 193), the first international labour standard devoted specifically to platform work. It examines the Convention's scope, substantive protections, and principal interpretive questions, arguing that its significance lies in the cumulative architecture through which platform work is brought within the reach of international labour standards. Particular attention is given to the Convention's broad personal scope. Self-employed platform workers are generally included throughout the instrument, while specific provisions permit protections to be adapted to different employment statuses without excluding workers outside an employment relationship. The analysis considers the Convention's provisions on fundamental principles and rights at work, occupational safety and health, violence and harassment, employment-status classification, remuneration, wage protection, social security, and the allocation of responsibility among platforms and intermediaries. This paper also examines the Convention's comparatively novel regulation of algorithmic management. It analyses rights to information concerning automated systems, the connection between their responsible use and collective bargaining, the concept of "decent work by design", written explanations and meaningful human review of automated decisions, personal-data protection, and safeguards concerning suspension, deactivation, and termination. Finally, the paper addresses applicable law, contractual circumvention, forum shopping, and access to remedies. Although the Convention reflects significant compromises, it fully recognises that platform work is work, extends labour protection into areas previously underdeveloped in international labour standards, and provides a binding foundation for national regulation, collective bargaining, litigation, enforcement, and further standard-setting.

title: When Talk is not Cheap: Communication and Agency Problems in LLM Agents

detail.title: When Talk is not Cheap: Communication and Agency Problems in LLM Agents
detail.abstract: AI agents are increasingly deployed in fiduciary roles on the premise that software has no private interests. We test this premise with 93 large language models in the trust game of Charness and Dufwenberg (2006) and a financial advising scenario with commission-driven conflicts. LLM agents systematically exploit principals under temptation, with cooperation falling from 58 to 20 percent as conflict intensity rises. Requiring a verbal promise before delegation raises cooperation by 13 to 17 percentage points, driven by independent guilt-aversion and lying-aversion channels. The dispositions are portable: trust-game promise violations predict risky-asset allocations, riskdownplaying, and transaction aggressiveness when advising a risk-averse retiree, with bunching at commission rates that meet sales targets. LLM principals over-trust exploitative counterparts, producing welfare losses that communication redistributes but does not correct. The findings imply that governing multi-agent AI systems requires not only aligning behavior, but also calibrating beliefs about strategically motivated counterparts.

title: AI Scribe technology improves efficiency of consultations in Dutch Primary Care: A real-world observational pre-post study

detail.title: AI Scribe technology improves efficiency of consultations in Dutch Primary Care: A real-world observational pre-post study
detail.abstract: BackgroundAdministrative burden contributes substantially to workload and burnout in primary care. AI-based voice-to-note tools (“AI scribes”) may reduce documentation time, but real-world evidence in primary care remains limited. We evaluated the impact of a Dutch-language AI scribe on consultation efficiency in routine primary care. MethodsWe conducted a prospective pre–post pilot study between December, 2024, and May, 2025, in 16 general practices in the province of Drenthe, the Netherlands. General practitioners (GPs) and nurse practitioners (NPs) registered 20 consecutive consultations before and after implementation of an AI scribe integrated with their electronic health record system. The primary outcome was the difference in the proportion of consultation time spent on administration (percentage points, 95% CI). Secondary outcomes were total consultation duration (seconds), administrative time (seconds), and number of clinical issues addressed. Linear mixed-effects models accounted for clustering within clinicians and practices. FindingsNineteen clinicians (14 GPs, five NPs) contributed 719 consultations (379 pre-use; 340 during use). The proportion of consultation time spent on administration decreased by 9,1 percentage points (95% CI −10,5 to −7,7). Administrative time decreased by 100 seconds (95% CI −116 to −84), and total consultation time decreased by 114 seconds (95% CI −176 to −53). The number of clinical issues addressed per consultation did not change (mean difference −0,02, 95% CI −0,10 to 0,05). Among GPs, administrative time proportion decreased from 27,8% to 17,4% (absolute difference −10,6 percentage points). Effects were independent of age and typing proficiency. InterpretationIn routine Dutch general practice, AI-supported documentation substantially reduced administrative workload and overall consultation time without reducing consultation content. Context-specific integration and evaluation after implementation may be key determinants of effectiveness. Larger controlled studies are needed to assess long-term sustainability, quality, patient experience, and cost-effectiveness. FundingNo commercial funding. The regional GP organisation facilitated participation through discounted access to the technology.

title: Come In: Comprehensive Care, Access Frictions, and Social Inclusion

detail.title: Come In: Comprehensive Care, Access Frictions, and Social Inclusion
detail.abstract: Even when a national minimum-income scheme formally exists, many eligible households fail to claim it or to benefit fully from it. We study ACCEDE—Spanish for “come in”—a clustered randomized controlled trial implemented by Cáritas across 64 parish clusters in Spain, alongside the national Minimum Income Scheme. Treated parishes opened a dedicated space offering personalized inclusion itineraries, benefit-claiming assistance, job-search and skills support, digital access, group activities, and intensive one-on-one accompaniment. Control parishes continued to provide Cáritas’s standard support. Both arms remained eligible for the same usual cash and in-kind material aid, so the experiment identifies the effect of the access and accompaniment bundle rather than the effect of additional transfers. The program increased average monthly household income, constructed from income received over the previous six months, by about 133 Euros, or 16 percent of the control-group mean. Intermediate outcomes point to several relaxed frictions: job-market engagement increased across employability measures, access to social rights improved, digital skills and connectivity rose, and participation in community groups increased by nearly half a standard deviation. We do not observe a corresponding improvement in regular contact and perceived support, and we cannot decompose the income gain into benefit take-up and earnings.The results nevertheless show that, even when a national income floor formally exists, informational, administrative, digital, and behavioral frictions can materially reduce its effective reach.

detail.abstract: Repugnance toward market transactions is often attributed to the nature of the goods exchanged. We study whether moral judgments are also shaped by contextual features-social proximity and the means of exchange. In a 2×2 between-subject experiment, participants evaluated ethically contentious transactions under family versus stranger and monetary versus non-monetary conditions, reporting personal and social norms on a four-point scale-"Normal," "Tolerable," "Distasteful," "Repugnant." We find that family ties had a stronger effect than monetary exchange. While money mainly shaped social acceptability, family involvement affected both norms. We also document heterogeneity across domains and context-dependent norm alignment.

title: Playing the Price: Informed Trading, Price Impact and Trade Splitting in Derivatives Markets

detail.title: Playing the Price: Informed Trading, Price Impact and Trade Splitting in Derivatives Markets
detail.abstract: This paper develops a simple game-theoretic model of informed trading, price impact, and trade splitting in derivatives markets. The model studies an informed trader who has a private valuation of a derivative contract and a market maker who adjusts execution prices in response to order size. In a one-period setting with linear price impact, the informed trader chooses an order quantity by balancing the value of an information edge against the cost of moving the price. The resulting optimal order size is increasing in the information edge and decreasing in the price-impact coefficient, while the equilibrium execution price lies halfway between the market maker's public-information valuation and the informed trader's private valuation. The paper then extends the model to a multi-period setting in which the informed trader splits trades across several rounds. Under linear permanent price impact, the optimal symmetric strategy is to trade equal quantities in each period. Total expected profit increases with the number of trading periods but converges to a finite upper bound, implying diminishing marginal gains from additional trade splitting. The framework provides a compact pedagogical link between adverse selection, market depth, and optimal execution in derivatives markets.

detail.abstract: One of the key institutions in a perpetual futures contract is the funding-rate mechanism, yet its role in information processing remains largely unexplored. This paper examines the question using the Binance XAUUSDT gold perpetual, a commodity-linked cryptocurrency perpetual introduced in January 2026, and 203,037 one-minute observations from its early trading period. In this benchmark-anchored instrument, whose reference value is discovered off-exchange, the order-flow proxies used in the paper have no unconditional predictive ability: trade-based order-flow imbalance is insignificant in-sample, produces negative outof-sample predictive R-squared, and fails to survive multiple-testing corrections. The active channel is instead the funding mechanism. The funding rate positively predicts returns at five-, fifteen-, and thirty-minute horizons (t = 2.22, 2.95, 3.71), while the funding-by-orderflow interaction is negative and significant at all three horizons (t =-2.64,-2.28,-2.26). The positive funding coefficient captures the persistence and directional component of leveragedriven demand, whereas the negative interaction captures the marginal reversal effect of additional buying pressure when positioning is already crowded. Session-level patterns around the European window are stable in sign but do not survive multiple-testing correction, alternative window definitions, alternative normalisations, or non-overlapping sampling schemes; event-study and placebo evidence do not isolate the London afternoon fix as the source of the pattern. The effects are small and not profitable once trading costs are considered. The evidence points to a funding-based positioning-and-reversal channel rather than a classical informed-trading channel in commodity-linked perpetuals.

detail.abstract:
Background. India has become a leading global supplier of affordable biologics, supported by large manufacturing capacity, cost competitiveness and a maturing scientific base. Yet domestic approval success does not translate automatically into sustained competitiveness in highly regulated markets, where post-marketing safety surveillance has become a central determinant of market access. 

Objective. This narrative review examines the pharmacovigilance (PV) challenges facing Indian biosimilar manufacturers as they expand into regulated markets, and considers how evolving regulatory expectations, real-world evidence (RWE) generation and artificial intelligence (AI) are reshaping the competitive landscape. 

Key challenges. Regulatory fragmentation, product-specific risk management plan (RMP) complexity, persistent traceability gaps at the batch level, long-horizon immunogenicity monitoring, cross-market signal detection, a deficit of multinational RWE, inspection readiness and a shortage of specialised PV expertise are identified as the principal barriers, with India-specific evidence on under-reporting and biologics surveillance presented to contextualise them. 

Future directions. A structured response is proposed through the GLOBAL-PV framework, anchored to specific regulatory instruments, alongside a discussion of AI-assisted case processing and its validation and governance requirements, and of patient-centric and ethical considerations. Recent regulatory developments including the United States Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) move to streamline biosimilar approval and converge biosimilarity with interchangeability are examined for their strategic implications. 

Conclusion. As analytical and manufacturing barriers narrow, pharmacovigilance excellence is emerging as the decisive differentiator. Indian manufacturers that embed robust safety surveillance, RWE generation, advanced signal detection and validated AI-enabled monitoring into their lifecycle strategy will be best positioned to lead in regulated international markets.

title: On the Failure of Representative-Agent Approximations

detail.title: On the Failure of Representative-Agent Approximations
detail.abstract: Representative-agent models are widely used as tractable approximations to heterogeneous economies. While classical aggregation theory identifies restrictive conditions under which heterogeneous agents can be represented exactly by a single agent, modern macroeconomic analysis often relies on a weaker claim: that representative-agent formulations provide useful local approximations to aggregate behavior. This paper examines that claim directly. We derive a general aggregation theorem showing that aggregation and differentiation do not generally commute. When individual decision rules are nonlinear in heterogeneous characteristics, the aggregate marginal response differs from the marginal response evaluated at average characteristics. The discrepancy is characterized by a covariance correction term involving the distribution of heterogeneous states and the curvature of the marginal response function. Consequently, representative-agent approximations fail generically whenever heterogeneity interacts with nonlinear marginal responses. The result identifies two knife-edge cases in which representative-agent approximations remain locally exact: homogeneous populations and locally linear marginal responses. Outside these special environments, aggregate comparative statics depend on distributional characteristics that cannot be recovered from average conditions alone. The theorem applies broadly to consumption, investment, expectations formation, labor supply, and other economic environments involving heterogeneous agents. The paper contributes to the aggregation literature by distinguishing the problem of aggregating marginal responses from the classical problem of aggregating levels. More generally, it identifies a class of environments in which heterogeneity remains aggregation-relevant and aggregate behavior depends directly on the distribution of underlying characteristics. The results imply that representative-agent models impose substantive restrictions on aggregate responses rather than serving as purely technical simplifications. More broadly, the theorem provides a general aggregation mechanism through which heterogeneity in decision architectures can influence aggregate outcomes, thereby contributing to the emerging literature on Hetero Behaviorus economies.

title: The Minimal Agency Condition: A Precondition for Welfare Evaluation

detail.title: The Minimal Agency Condition: A Precondition for Welfare Evaluation
detail.abstract: This paper argues that normative welfare economics presupposes a Minimal Agency Condition (MAC). Although preference-based and opportunity-based approaches disagree regarding the appropriate metric of welfare, both rely upon the assumption that individuals possess sufficient practical agency for preferences or opportunities to function as meaningful indicators of well-being. I argue that this presupposition has received insufficient explicit attention. The paper develops the concept of survival-dominant compression, whereby severe deprivation may systematically narrow practical agency through the dominance of immediate stabilization pressures. Under such conditions, preferences and opportunities may remain observable while their connection to welfare becomes increasingly unstable. The resulting problem is not merely one of imperfect information or behavioral distortion. Rather, welfare metrics themselves may lose the interpretive authority required to support normative welfare claims. MAC identifies the minimal level of practical agency necessary for welfare metrics to function as normatively interpretable indicators of well-being. The argument differs from capability theories, adaptive preference critiques, and behavioral welfare economics by focusing not on the content of welfare or preferences, but on the applicability conditions of welfare metrics themselves. The paper concludes that the traditional preference-opportunity debate is methodologically incomplete unless the practical conditions required for welfare interpretation are explicitly specified. MAC is proposed as one such condition. This manuscript is the first in a planned research program developing the Minimal Agency Condition (MAC) and exploring its implications for welfare economics, behavioral welfare theory, contractarian justification, responsibility attribution, market legitimacy, and democratic theory.

This paper studies a portfolio-construction method that imposes factor neutrality directly on implemented capital weights, rather than only residualising the alpha signal before optimisation. At each rebalance, portfolios are represented in coordinates inside the monitored neutral subspace, making the final traded portfolio factor-neutral by construction. The method is equivalent to equality-constrained Markowitz optimisation and gives finite-sample leakage bounds when exposure definitions differ.

The construction is extended to projected partial rebalancing, where the previous holding is first projected into the current neutral subspace and then moved part way toward the full neutral target. Walk-forward tests across six research universes show numerical-level exposure leakage for neutral-coordinate portfolios and lower turnover for projected partial variants.

Afghan women’s and girls’ lack of access to education and health services and denial of their freedom of movement threaten to increase maternal mortality thus denying them their human rights. 

This article synthesizes recent peer-reviewed studies and institutional reports on maternal mortality following the Taliban’s return to power in Afghanistan in August 2021 and compares emerging patterns with the first Taliban period (1996–2001), when maternal mortality reached some of the highest levels recorded in conflict settings.

Multiple data sources indicate worsening conditions after 2021, including sharp reductions in service utilization following funding interruptions, reported declines in access to antenatal and intrapartum care, and clinician-reported increases in delays and life-threatening obstetric complications. Modelling based on routine health data suggests that sustained reductions in coverage could result in thousands of additional maternal deaths annually.

The acute difference between Afghanistan especially since 2021 and many other fragile settings is that gender-based restrictions specifically target women’s and girls’ education, employment, and movement, directly affecting demand-side access and supply-side staffing capacity for maternal care, thus offending Afghanistan’s obligations under the Convention on the Elimination of All forms of Discrimination against Women.

detail.abstract: Federal broadband programs are promoted partly on rural-health grounds, yet credibly identified evidence on whether broadband improves rural health is scarce, and the $42 billion BEAD program makes the question pressing. This study estimates the short-run association between the 2009 federal broadband stimulus (the USDA Broadband Initiatives Program and the NTIA Broadband Technology Opportunities Program) and a battery of rural health and socioeconomic outcomes. A rejected-applicant differencein-differences design compares 2,448 funded counties to 263 trajectory-matched rejected applicants, contrasting the pre-award (2010-2013) and pre-COVID post-award (2018-2019) periods. I estimate effects on nineteen County Health Rankings outcomes spanning healthcare access, screening, health behaviors, mortality, mental health, and socioeconomic status, with cluster-robust, randomization-inference, family-wise falsediscovery-rate, and state-by-year fixed-effects checks. The award raised fiber availability by 2.8 percentage points relative to rejected applicants, yet I find no robust effect on any of the nineteen outcomes. The two conventionally significant baseline estimates (preventable hospitalizations and high-school graduation) are absorbed by state-byyear fixed effects, consistent with state-level confounding, though that specification may also absorb state-level treatment variation; child poverty survives that test but not a multiple-testing correction, and the rest are precise nulls with reported minimum detectable effects. The stimulus raised fiber availability only modestly, and that expansion produced no detectable short-run improvements in rural health or socioeconomic outcomes. The estimates bound the short-run health returns to a 2.8-percentage-point fiber increase below policy-relevant magnitudes, an input to the cost-benefit case for the far larger BEAD program.

title: Distress, Not Just Drugs: NAFTA, Suicide, and the Geography of the Opioid Epidemic

detail.title: Distress, Not Just Drugs: NAFTA, Suicide, and the Geography of the Opioid Epidemic

detail.abstract: How do trade shocks raise mortality, and through which causes of death? Using restricted, county-identified CDC Multiple Cause of Death microdata for 1990 to 2024 and the Hakobyan and McLaren county tariff shift-share, I find that the mortality response to NAFTA runs through suicide rather than through the drug overdoses of the contemporaneous opioid epidemic. A one-standard-deviation increase in exposure raises the age-adjusted suicide rate by 0.30 to 0.53 per 100,000. The estimate holds under a China-shock control, division-by-year fixed effects, commuting-zone trends, and spatial-HAC inference, though it is marginal under the most demanding shockpermutation test. Drug overdose shows no robust positive response: it is imprecise, halved by within-state fixed effects, and negative in the fentanyl era. The suicide response survives excluding every drug-related death and is carried by firearm suicide, which rises even where prescription opioids were scarce, both in the states whose pre-1996 triplicate-prescription programs held down OxyContin and across the county distribution of opioid shipments. Firearm suicide is therefore not the opioid epidemic completed by a firearm. The response is borne by men and concentrated among non-Hispanic whites, and a labor-market first stage confirms that exposure depressed local employment and income. Because the scar persists and no later trade-policy episode reverses it, the policy margin is local labor markets and mental-health infrastructure, not the trade barrier itself.

detail.abstract: We present a regime-split Black-Scholes implied volatility solver in which every initial seed is a fully closed-form analytical expression, derived from the asymptotic structure of the Black-Scholes price in its natural domain. At the money, series reversion of an exact Gaussian identity yields a fourth-order seed with error O(s 8). In the moderate out-of-the-money region, successive Gaussian CDF approximations of increasing order produce explicit initial seed formulas whose accuracy is proved numerically, with no iteration or numerical inversion at the seed stage. In the deep out-of-the-money region, a Gaussian tail cancellation identity-the Mills ratio-reveals the asymptotic structure of the Black-Scholes price and motivates a ratio-corrected seed that achieves near-machine-precision initialisation for large moneyness. All regime boundaries are derived analytically from CDF truncation tolerances and numerical solver theoretical error bounds, with no empirically tuned constants. A universal fourth-order Householder polisher then drives all regimes to machine precision, with mean update iterations strictly below two on both standard and granular benchmark grids-meeting and surpassing the two-iteration target established by the highest-accuracy reference implementations in the literature. The resulting C implementation achieves a 1.73-1.78× throughput gain over the state-of-the-art benchmark under identical hardware and compiler conditions, with maximum absolute error O(10-14), stable across grid configurations. A Python/Numba implementation confirms portability. All source code is publicly available.

title: Seven Structural Threats Reshaping the Insurance Industry: Insurability, the Customer Relationship, and the Balance Sheet

detail.title: Seven Structural Threats Reshaping the Insurance Industry: Insurability, the Customer Relationship, and the Balance Sheet
detail.abstract: The global insurance industry is being reshaped by a convergence of structural pressures that, taken together, alter the fundamentals of the business: what insurers can price, who owns the customer relationship, and who owns the risk capital that backs policies. This paper offers an analytical review of seven contemporary threats and organizes them into three categories. Threats to insurability-climate risk and home affordability are compressing the set of risks that private markets can profitably underwrite. Threats to the customer relationship-the erosion of consumer trust, the entry of original-equipment manufacturers (OEMs) into auto insurance, and artificial intelligence are contesting who intermediates between insurer and insured. Threats to the balance sheet-private-equity consolidation of life insurers and a tightening regulatory environment are changing who holds and governs insurance capital. Drawing on peer-reviewed research and authoritative 2024-2026 industry and regulatory data, the paper argues that these threats are interdependent rather than isolated, and that the industry's response to any one of them is constrained by the others. It identifies the mechanisms linking the seven threats and outlines implications for insurers, regulators, and policyholders.

title: Hetero Behaviorus Dynamics

detail.title: Hetero Behaviorus Dynamics
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes how heterogeneous behavioral architectures can affect aggregate economic dynamics. Standard dynamic models typically characterize stability, trajectories, and long-run behavior using economic fundamentals such as preferences, technologies, endowments, and policy rules. In representativeagent settings, differences in expectation formation, information processing, learning, forecasting, attention, and inference are either abstracted away or treated as dynamically irrelevant. This paper examines the consequences of allowing the distribution of behavioral architectures to enter the aggregate state description. The analysis introduces behavioral composition as a potential state variable and studies dynamic systems in which aggregate outcomes depend jointly on economic conditions and the distribution of behavioral architectures. The central result is a Behavioral Stability Theorem. The theorem establishes that behavioral composition may alter the local stability properties of an economy even when underlying economic fundamentals remain unchanged. Consequently, two economies with identical preferences, technologies, endowments, policy rules, and structural parameters may exhibit different dynamic behavior solely because they possess different distributions of behavioral architectures. Several implications follow. Behavioral composition may alter aggregate trajectories despite identical fundamentals, generate bifurcations without changes in structural parameters, and create path dependence through the evolution of behavioral distributions. These results imply that behavioral heterogeneity may influence not only aggregate outcomes but also the dynamic structure through which those outcomes evolve. The paper therefore identifies conditions under which distributions of behavioral architectures constitute economically meaningful state variables rather than merely descriptive characteristics of a population.

title: Compensation vs. Reinforcement: Experimental Identification of Parental Aversion to Inequality in Offspring
affiliations: Department of Economics, Harvard University - Harvard Graduate School of Education, Central Bank of Colombia, Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), Kyoto University, Catholic University of Lille - IESEG School of Management and University of Arizona

detail.title: Compensation vs. Reinforcement: Experimental Identification of Parental Aversion to Inequality in Offspring
detail.abstract: Parents may invest differently across children by compensating the disadvantaged child or by reinforcing the child with higher expected returns. We study this question using a conditional cash transfer experiment that uniquely randomized transfers at the student level, generating exogenous variation in transfer exposure across siblings within the same household. The transfers increased short-run attendance among treated students but generated negative spillovers on untreated siblings: untreated siblings of treated students were 3.7 percentage points less likely to graduate from college, a decline of about 30 percent relative to the control mean. We interpret these effects using a dynamic model of household schooling decisions that identifies parental aversion to inequality in children's educational outcomes. The estimated model implies limited aversion to inequality in children's educational outcomes and reproduces held-out treatment effects not used in estimation. A decomposition shows that the negative spillover is primarily driven by substitution in educational investments toward the treated child.

title: Where Overheating Sits: A Derived Household-Welfare Localization of Sectoral Fragility

detail.title: Where Overheating Sits: A Derived Household-Welfare Localization of Sectoral Fragility

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a closed input-output method for locating financial overheating within the productive and household structure of an economy, distinguishing where overheating sits from how large it is. Embedding sectoral overheating in a closed Leontief system with a household income-consumption loop of the Miyazawa type, I derive-rather than assign-sectoral loss weights as the shadow price of a household-welfare loss functional propagated through the closed inverse. The resulting sectoral household-welfare loss multiplier, and a localization index built from it, admit a scale-invariant decomposition: at equal aggregate overheating, fragility rises with the covariance between the sectoral distribution of overheating and the household-welfare transmission profile. In a leakage-free accounting benchmark, a structural identity, v ⊤ (I-A)-1 = 1 ⊤, makes value-added weights near-degenerate for localization and collapses the value-added and labor profiles onto a single affine family; the two separate only through accounting leakage or heterogeneous shock sensitivity, while the welfare projection carries information neither standard weight can. A threshold mechanism renders concentration in welfare-critical, high-transmission sectors costly through a piecewise-linear activation channel. On real input-output tables for eight European economies, welfare weighting separates a housing-credit boom from a manufacturing boom several times more sharply than value-added weighting, while labor weighting does not even order the two consistently; and the open value-added projection loosens with import openness exactly as the leakage accounting predicts. The corresponding cross-country severity test-contrasting welfare weights with value-added, labor, and output-centrality weights, conditional on a pre-specified weight-distinguishability check-is set out as a prospective design for future estimation rather than a completed test.

detail.abstract: We provide the first separate estimates of the independent demand effects of Australia's two main private health insurance (PHI) instruments: the Medicare Levy Surcharge (MLS), a tax penalty for uninsured higher-income individuals, and the PHI rebate, an income-and age-differentiated premium subsidy. Prior work estimated only bundled effects because the 2012 reform moved MLS and rebate thresholds jointly. We exploit the fact that rebate rates vary not just by income but, for given income, by age and over fiscal years, enabling separate GMM identification of MLS and rebate effects using linked administrative tax and Medicare data from the Person Level Integrated Data Asset (2010-2020). Our jointly estimated effects allow us, for the first time, to assess the relative importance of penalty and subsidy incentives on PHI demand and fiscal balance. We present counterfactual experiments assessing budget-neutral simultaneous changes to both instruments that raise population PHI coverage. Our estimates are directly applicable to recent proposals to equalise PHI rebate rates across age groups: equalising at the under-65 rate would reduce PHI take-up among older Australians modestly, with fiscal savings accruing primarily through reduced payments to infra-marginal existing policyholders.

detail.abstract: Global imbalances are once again moving to the center of the international economic debate. But today’s imbalances are not simply a replay of the pre-global financial crisis period. Two decades ago, the main concern was whether large current account surpluses in emerging Asia and oil-exporting economies, matched by persistent U.S. deficits, would end in a disorderly adjustment of exchange rates, asset prices, and global demand. detail.title: Trading Frictions in Dynamic Cap-and-Trade Markets
detail.abstract: We develop a dynamic stochastic model of markets with an externality and multiple trading frictions, and cap-and-trade as the leading application. Slow participation, limited intermediation, and heterogeneous information interact in equilibrium: agents choose costly market access, access determines residual compliance demand, intermediary constraints translate residual demand into a surrender-month premium, and the premium feeds back into access incentives. These interactions shape how effectively the market corrects the externality. We characterize access choices in closed form, prove that the equilibrium premium is unique, and show that endogenous access dampens the response to each friction in isolation, while the interaction of multiple frictions is non-additive and can amplify the price response. We quantify the model using 2.7 million EU ETS registry transactions and compliance records from 2005-2021. About 40% of operators do not trade annually, purchases concentrate in April when returns are systematically high, and operator flow predicts future returns.

detail.abstract: Japan’s policy toward foreign residents is shifting toward stronger regulation. As of the end of June 2025, the number of foreign residents in Japan stood at 3,956,619, roughly double the figure recorded in 2004. The number of foreign nationals entering Japan in 2024 also reached an all-time high of approximately 36.78 million. Alongside this quantitative increase, the long-term settlement of foreign residents has also been rising. The number of long-term residents in Japan—including permanent residents, spouses or children of Japanese nationals, spouses or children of permanent residents, long-term residents, and special permanent residents—increased from approximately 1.36 million, or 66.7 percent of all foreign residents, at the end of December 2012 to approximately 1.64 million, or 41.3 percent, at the end of June 2025. Looking only at permanent residents among these long-term residents, their number rose from 620,000 to 930,000 over the same period, an increase of roughly 310,000.

detail.abstract: Horizontal inequity occurs when employees and self-employed with the same income end up with different effective tax burdens, due to the difficulty of enforcing taxes on self-employed. Based on detailed micro-tax simulations models integrated with household surveys in 29 developing countries, we show that tax systems incur large horizontal inequities in practice and that reforms which improve vertical equity worsen horizontal equity by a comparable amount. An in-person survey in Pakistan and online surveys across multiple countries reveal widespread concern about horizontal equity. Randomized information treatments heighten this concern but do not shift tax preferences toward addressing horizontal inequity.

title: Designed for Whom? Spatial Inequity, Settlement Dynamics, and Newcomer Exclusion from Community Circular Economy Infrastructure
